posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Packachu said:
I've tried going into device manager and uninstalling the display driver there, and going into settings and deleting the application, then restarting my pc.
Click to expand...
This is not actually a good way to handle removing drivers because they operate at a pretty low level in the operating system. It's better to use a specific utility, such as DDU.
DDU'ing your display driver (which, DDU = Display Driver Uninstaller) will give you a truly clean removal and reinstallation of the GPU driver. Maybe worth considering doing now that you have removed the display drivers through device manager, but if there are no graphical errors or low graphical performance problems, this is barking up the wrong tree.
It was worth troubleshooting these steps, but I'd say that display driver isn't the problem. If you can launch literally any other game, this isn't the problem. MV/MZ games really do not utilize the display driver very much at all - MZ does use it more than MV, but it's still marginal.
Packachu said:
I've reinstalled the new driver, it brings up
Click to expand...
This is just an NWJS profile error and it's basically saying that the profile on your computer does not match the version of the game's version of NWJS. This error can be safely ignored. It is a common warning for people who play a lot of MV/MZ games.

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
@TheAM-Dol
Package.json is not empty in a deployed game. The name field is. nw.js uses name field to access uer data of the app. If OP once ran an nw.js app with an empty name, it will try to read data from the default nwjs folder (insde your user profile/appdata/local folder), it will cause problems sometimes.  There were topics talked about games with wrong icons because the developer left the name field empty.

Since the more complex solutions make no difference, I would like to check a few basic assumptions that (at least from what I read) haven't been checked so far:
1) when you extract those games, what is the exact and full folderpath where you extract them to?
At best, test it with something simple like c:\gamename
This is to make sure that you don't accidentally extracted it into a folder that has problems like being restricted or containing a forbidden letter in the name.
2) how exactly did you try to launch the game?
